argument_summary: The admissible record supports only a limited certification theory: aggregate readiness passed by 2.2 points, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and deployment includes staged rollout, rollback, and monitoring. But the construction site safety segment remains below target, remains exposed in the initial cohort, and there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. On this record, the defensible position is not that the weakness is resolved or that rollout controls eliminate it, but that certification is supportable only if the unresolved construction site safety limitation is explicitly disclosed as part of launch governance.
claims_about_business_cost: A full escalation on the theory that rollout controls are being misrepresented would be broader than the admissible record warrants if the packet is narrowed to the disclosure-based certification theory. The record does show meaningful readiness and deployment controls, so the practical governance question is whether certification is framed with the required limitation disclosure, not whether the launch is entirely unsupported.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy cuts against any clean claim that rollout controls alone cure the issue. The policy says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and the policy text further says that a rollback switch, dashboard, or small initial percentage does not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed. Because the exposed construction site safety segment is neither excluded nor covered by approved risk acceptance, the supportable policy position is caveated compliance through explicit disclosure, not unconditional compliance.
concessions: The construction site safety segment remains below target on incident-report severity routing and is still eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
The current risk acceptance draft is incomplete, unapproved, and does not address the construction site safety exposure.
The present record does not support a claim that rollout controls by themselves satisfy the disclosure policy.
The present record also does not include the actual model-card or release artifact proving the required disclosure has been prepared and bound to launch.
